strengths: Novel contribution: the paper claims (and substantiates) the first training-free approach to use discrete diffusion models (VQ-Diffusion, and later a masked generative motion model) as priors for solving linear inverse problems, addressing the non-differentiability issue via a variational categorical distribution and Gumbel-Softmax continuous relaxation.

Solid theoretical development: Theorem 3.1 (ELBO-style bound on marginal KL) and Lemma 3.2 (decomposition into prior-fit and likelihood terms) are proven in detail in the appendix, giving the method a principled derivation rather than being purely heuristic.

Good diagnostic motivation: Figure 2 clearly demonstrates the practical problem with mask-absorbing discrete diffusion (early-committed structure that cannot be revised), which motivates the star-shaped noise process solution; the graphical-model ablation (G2D2 vs. G2D2 w/ Markov noise process) empirically supports that the star-shaped process is responsible for most of the gains.

Reasonably comprehensive empirical evaluation across two tasks (super-resolution, Gaussian deblurring) on two datasets (ImageNet, FFHQ), against four representative baselines spanning pixel-domain and latent diffusion methods, plus a qualitative extension to motion path-following with a discrete masked generative model, showing some generality beyond images.
Practical efficiency: G2D2 has notably lower GPU memory usage than all compared methods and reasonable runtime, which is a meaningful practical advantage for a gradient-guided approach.
Reproducibility effort: detailed hyperparameters, learning-rate/KL scheduling, and algorithm boxes are provided in the appendix, and the authors state intent to release code.
weaknesses: The central empirical claim is only that G2D2 is 'comparable' to continuous-domain methods, not that it outperforms them; on FFHQ in particular, pixel-domain methods (DDRM, DPS) clearly and consistently outperform G2D2 by sizeable PSNR/LPIPS margins, which somewhat undercuts the practical significance of the contribution.

Confounded comparison: G2D2 uses a different pretrained backbone (VQ-Diffusion trained on ITHQ) than the baselines (trained on ImageNet/FFHQ directly), which the authors acknowledge but which makes head-to-head numeric comparisons less conclusive — differences could stem from prior quality/domain mismatch rather than the proposed algorithm per se.

Evaluation scale is modest (100 images per dataset/task, only two linear tasks), and no quantitative metrics are reported for the motion inverse problem experiment (only qualitative figures), which weakens the evidentiary support for the claimed cross-domain generality.

The method's applicability is restricted to linear inverse problems and models resembling mask-absorbing discrete diffusion/MaskGIT-style architectures; nonlinear operators and other discrete diffusion parameterizations (e.g., non-absorbing transition matrices, continuous-time discrete diffusion) are not explored, despite being mentioned as important use cases in the introduction.

Limited ablation/sensitivity analysis on key design choices such as the number of optimization iterations, Gumbel-Softmax temperature, and the substitution of the true q(z0|zt) with the pretrained model output p̃θ(z0|zt) in Lemma 3.2 (an approximation whose looseness is not empirically quantified).

The paper does not report variance/confidence intervals across the 100-image test sets, making it hard to assess the statistical significance of the reported PSNR/LPIPS differences, especially where G2D2 is close to or behind baselines.

strengths: First work to tackle image linear inverse problems using discrete (VQ-Diffusion) priors, addressing a genuine gap since prior gradient-guided inverse-problem methods (DPS, PSLD, etc.) assume differentiable continuous latents.

Identifies a concrete and well-illustrated failure mode of mask-absorbing discrete diffusion for inverse problems (early-step errors become uncorrectable because unmasked tokens cannot revert), supported by an informative preliminary experiment (Fig. 2).

The star-shaped noise process fix is theoretically motivated: the paper proves (Theorem 3.1, Lemma 3.2, and supporting lemmas in the appendix) that the variational marginal is bounded by a sum of per-step KL terms, and that the sampling marginal matches the true posterior, giving the method a principled basis rather than being purely heuristic.

The ablation between the star-shaped and Markov noise variants (Table 1, 2, Figs. 12-13) convincingly demonstrates the practical benefit of the proposed re-masking-enabling process, isolating this specific contribution.

Reasonably broad empirical validation: two datasets (ImageNet, FFHQ), two tasks (SR, deblurring), comparison against representative pixel- and latent-diffusion baselines, plus a cross-domain demonstration on discrete motion generation (MMM) for path-conditioned generation, showing some generality of the framework.
Reports compute/memory footprint (Table 4), showing G2D2 is relatively lightweight compared to other gradient-guided baselines (PSLD, ReSample, DPS).
weaknesses: The central empirical claim is that G2D2 performs 'comparably' to continuous diffusion methods, but the tables show it is frequently outperformed (sometimes clearly, e.g., DDRM on FFHQ deblurring: 31.12 vs 26.35 PSNR) and rarely, if ever, the best method — this raises the question of what practical benefit the added complexity (variational optimization + Gumbel-Softmax relaxation at every step) provides over simply using an existing continuous prior when one is available.

Baselines and G2D2 use different pre-trained backbones (different training data, model capacity, architecture), which the authors themselves note 'contributes to the superiority of pixel-domain methods on FFHQ' — this confound substantially undermines the validity of head-to-head PSNR/LPIPS comparisons as evidence of methodological superiority or parity.

Evaluation is limited to only 100 images per dataset/task with no reported variance, confidence intervals, or statistical significance testing, making the reported gaps between methods hard to interpret reliably.

Task diversity is narrow — only two linear tasks (SR, Gaussian deblurring); no inpainting, phase retrieval, or nonlinear settings, despite related continuous-diffusion baselines (DPS) supporting broader tasks, limiting demonstrated generality claimed in the introduction.

The motion-domain experiment (Section 4.4) is purely qualitative (a single figure), with no quantitative metrics (e.g., path-following error, motion realism/FID) to substantiate the claim of successful path-conditioned generation, weakening this secondary contribution.

The key approximation in Lemma 3.2 — substituting the pretrained model p̃θ(z0|zt) for the intractable true q(z0|zt) — is a reasonable but unproven heuristic substitution; its approximation error is not analyzed or bounded, so the theoretical guarantee (Theorem 3.1) does not fully carry over to the practical algorithm.

Contribution is largely a combination of existing techniques (star-shaped/decoupled noise process from Okhotin et al. and Zhang et al., Gumbel-Softmax relaxation, VQ-Diffusion/MaskGIT priors) applied to a new setting, which somewhat limits methodological novelty despite being a useful synthesis.

Computational cost, while lower than some latent-diffusion baselines, is still substantially higher than DDRM (194s vs 4s) for comparable or worse quality, and the paper's own limitations section acknowledges no clear speed or performance advantage over continuous counterparts.

strengths: Novel and clearly motivated contribution: to the authors' knowledge, this is the first method enabling discrete diffusion models (e.g., VQ-Diffusion) to be used as training-free priors for continuous-space linear inverse problems, addressing a genuine gap left by prior work that either required additional trained networks or was confined to low-dimensional/inpainting-only settings.

Strong theoretical grounding: the paper provides a variational upper bound (Theorem 3.1) connecting the marginal KL divergence between the approximate and true posterior to a sum of per-step KL divergences, along with a clean decomposition (Lemma 3.2) into prior-consistency and likelihood terms; full proofs are given in the appendix, including the identity between qsampling and the true posterior marginal.

Good diagnostic analysis: Figure 2 convincingly demonstrates the core issue with mask-absorbing discrete diffusion (image structure is fixed within the first ~10% of steps), which motivates and justifies the star-shaped noise process solution.

Solid empirical validation of the key design choice: the ablation between the proposed star-shaped noise process and a Markov-noise variant (Tables 1–2, Figures 12–13) clearly shows the star-shaped process is necessary and effective, closing much of the gap to continuous diffusion baselines.

Reasonably comprehensive experiments across modalities: image super-resolution and Gaussian deblurring on ImageNet/FFHQ, plus a proof-of-concept extension to motion data (path-following with MMM) demonstrating cross-domain applicability without additional training.
Practical efficiency: Table 4 shows G2D2 has the lowest GPU memory footprint among compared methods and competitive runtime versus other gradient-guided approaches (DPS, PSLD, ReSample).

Strong reproducibility effort: extensive appendix detailing hyperparameters, scheduling formulas, forward-operator implementations, and comparison-method settings, with a stated intent to release code.
weaknesses: G2D2 does not outperform continuous-domain methods; it is only described as 'comparable,' and in several FFHQ metrics (e.g., DDRM) it trails by a non-trivial margin, somewhat limiting the significance of the contribution despite its novelty.

Baselines and G2D2 use different underlying pretrained generative models (VQ-Diffusion-ITHQ vs. guided-diffusion vs. Stable Diffusion vs. LDM-VQ), which the authors acknowledge affects fairness of comparison and makes it hard to isolate the effect of the proposed algorithm versus prior model quality.

Evaluation is restricted to two linear tasks (SR and Gaussian deblurring) on 100 images per dataset; broader inverse problems (inpainting, colorization, more diverse degradations, higher noise levels) and larger evaluation sets would strengthen the empirical claims.

The motion-data experiment (Section 4.4) is only qualitative (Figure 14), with no quantitative metrics (e.g., path-following error, motion realism/FID) to substantiate the claimed success of the discrete-prior application in this domain.

The paper is explicit that G2D2 does not surpass continuous counterparts in speed or performance and defers nonlinear inverse problems and other modalities (audio/video) to future work, meaning the current scope is somewhat narrow relative to the broader promise implied by the framing.

Sensitivity/robustness analysis is limited to the forget coefficient (Appendix C.6); there is little exploration of sensitivity to the number of diffusion steps T, classifier-free guidance scale, or measurement noise level, which would help establish robustness of the method.

strengths: Addresses a genuinely underexplored problem: using discrete diffusion models (e.g., VQ-Diffusion, masked generative motion models) as priors for training-free linear inverse problem solving, overcoming non-differentiability via a variational categorical distribution optimized with Gumbel-Softmax relaxation.

The identification and fix of the mask-absorbing 'frozen error' problem via a star-shaped noise process is a clear, well-motivated methodological contribution, supported by an intuitive theoretical decomposition (qstar-decomp) with a proven marginal-preservation property and a KL upper-bound theorem justifying the variational approximation.

Thorough ablation isolates the benefit of the star-shaped process versus a Markov-noise variant, showing large, consistent gains on both ImageNet and FFHQ (Tables 1-2), and qualitative results (Fig. 4, 14, 15) convincingly illustrate the re-masking/error-correction mechanism.

Strong practical benefit demonstrated: substantially lower GPU memory (4.7 GiB vs 10.7-20.9 GiB for DPS/PSLD) while achieving performance broadly comparable to continuous-domain baselines on LPIPS/PSNR.

Good breadth of experiments and reproducibility effort: two datasets, two tasks, several baselines, additional metrics (SSIM/FID/KID) and multiple appendix ablations (forget coefficient, text-conditioning impact, prior model choice, failure-mode analysis), plus a demonstration of applicability to a non-image domain (motion generation with MMM) without additional training.
Honest discussion of limitations (linear-only setting, prompt-data mismatch failure cases, room for improvement in motion trajectory accuracy) rather than overstating results.
weaknesses: The headline claim of 'comparable performance' to continuous diffusion baselines is only supported by LPIPS/PSNR; the appendix's own FID/KID numbers (Tables 8-11) frequently show G2D2 noticeably worse than DPS and sometimes PSLD, which tempers the main quantitative claim and should be reflected more prominently in the main text rather than relegated to the appendix.

Cross-method comparisons are confounded by using different pretrained backbones (VQ-Diffusion/ITHQ for G2D2 vs. ImageNet/FFHQ-specific pixel and latent diffusion models for baselines), making it hard to attribute performance differences to the proposed method itself rather than to prior quality/training data mismatch (acknowledged by the authors but not fully controlled for).

In the motion inverse problem experiment, G2D2 substantially underperforms fine-tuned baselines (OmniControl, GMD) on trajectory and location error metrics (e.g., Traj. Err 0.272 vs 0.053), a much larger gap than in the image domain, suggesting the star-shaped/variational approach may generalize less well to this setting or that the task is a weaker demonstration of applicability.

Wall-clock speed advantage over DPS is modest (194s vs 277s per image) despite the large memory reduction, so the primary practical benefit is narrower (memory) than the abstract's framing might suggest.

The theoretical guarantee (Theorem 3.1) bounds a KL divergence via a sum of per-step terms, but the practical objective substitutes the pretrained denoiser p̃θ for the true qstar(z0|zt) and relies on Gumbel-Softmax approximation of the likelihood term; the paper does not analyze how tight the bound is in practice or how bias from these substitutions/relaxations affects sample quality, leaving a gap between the theory and the practical algorithm.

Results and hyperparameters (e.g., KL weighting schedules, forget coefficient, text prompts) appear to require nontrivial per-task/per-dataset tuning (Table 4), and the failure-mode analysis shows sensitivity to prompt/data mismatch, indicating potential brittleness of the approach outside the tested settings.

strengths: Addresses a genuine and underexplored gap: applying discrete diffusion models (VQ-Diffusion, MaskGIT-style masked generative models) as priors for continuous linear inverse problems via a variational continuous relaxation, which is technically non-trivial given the non-differentiable codebook/argmax operations in discrete diffusion.

Provides a clear theoretical justification chain: definition of a star-decomposed distribution that provably preserves the marginal posterior of the star-shaped process (Lemma D.1), and an ELBO-style upper bound (Theorem 3.1) decomposed into prior-fit and likelihood terms (Lemma 3.1), giving the variational optimization a principled basis rather than being purely heuristic.

The ablation comparing the proposed star-shaped noise process against a Markov noise process variant is convincing and isolates the contribution of the re-masking mechanism, showing a large, consistent improvement across both datasets and both tasks.

Reasonably broad empirical validation: two datasets (ImageNet, FFHQ), two tasks (SR, deblurring), multiple strong baselines (DPS, DDRM, PSLD, ReSample), additional appendix metrics (SSIM/FID/KID), hyperparameter and prior-choice ablations, a documented failure-mode analysis, and an out-of-image-domain demonstration (motion path-following) showing some generality of the framework.

Reports GPU memory and wall-clock comparisons showing a substantial and practically relevant memory reduction relative to gradient-based baselines, which is a real practical benefit if verified fairly.
weaknesses: The central claim of 'comparable performance to continuous diffusion techniques' is only supported by LPIPS/PSNR in the main tables; the FID/KID numbers relegated to the appendix (Tables 8-11) frequently show G2D2 performing considerably worse than DPS and sometimes PSLD (e.g., FFHQ SR FID 45.21 for G2D2 vs 26.85 for DPS, KID 3.08 vs 0.67), which undercuts the paper's headline claim and suggests the perceptually favorable LPIPS numbers do not tell the whole story.

The cross-method comparisons are confounded because each baseline uses a different pretrained backbone (different training data, architecture, and capacity for DPS/DDRM/PSLD/ReSample/G2D2). Consequently, differences in memory usage, speed, and quality could be attributable largely to the choice of underlying prior model rather than to the proposed algorithmic contribution, and this confound is not adequately controlled for or discussed as a limitation.

The core methodological novelty is somewhat incremental: the star-shaped noise process is directly imported from prior continuous-diffusion works (Okhotin et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2024), and the Gumbel-Softmax relaxation for making discrete generation differentiable is a well-known technique; the paper's contribution is largely the combination/adaptation of existing tools to a new setting rather than a fundamentally new technique.

On the motion inverse-problem task, G2D2 substantially underperforms fine-tuned baselines on the most task-relevant metrics (trajectory error 0.272 vs 0.053 for OmniControl, an ~5x gap; location error similarly much worse), which weakens the claimed generality of the approach beyond images, even though the authors frame this as an unfair comparison against fine-tuned methods.

The method's practical usability is limited by dataset/task-specific hyperparameter tuning (distinct learning-rate and KL-weight schedules per task/dataset in Table 4) and prompt-dependence, with the failure-mode analysis (Appendix E.9) showing that prompt/target mismatches produce visible artifacts that the star-shaped re-masking cannot always correct, suggesting sensitivity and lack of robustness that is not fully resolved.

Only linear inverse problems and Gaussian-noise likelihoods are addressed; nonlinear inverse problems, which are common and often more interesting for the diffusion-posterior-sampling literature, are left entirely to future work, limiting the scope of the demonstrated contribution.

strengths: Addresses a genuine and previously under-explored gap: enabling gradient-based, training-free posterior sampling with discrete diffusion priors for continuous-space inverse problems, via a principled continuous relaxation (Gumbel-Softmax) of a variational categorical posterior.

The star-shaped noise process is a well-motivated fix for the mask-absorbing limitation (inability to 're-mask'/correct early errors), and the paper backs this up both theoretically (star-decomposed distribution with proven marginal equivalence, Theorem 3.1/Lemma 3.1, full proofs in Appendix D) and empirically (Fig. 2 and 4 demonstrations, ablation in Table 1/2 showing large gains over the Markov-noise variant).

Comprehensive empirical validation across two image tasks (SR, deblurring) on two datasets (ImageNet, FFHQ) against four strong baselines (DPS, DDRM, PSLD, ReSample), plus an entirely different modality (motion path-following with MMM) showing the method generalizes to masked generative models without retraining.

Practically meaningful efficiency result: G2D2 matches continuous-diffusion-based methods within a small LPIPS/PSNR margin while cutting GPU memory by up to ~77% (4.7GiB vs 20.9GiB for PSLD), enabling use on consumer 8GiB GPUs — a concrete, well-quantified advantage (Table 5).

Extensive and honest ablations/ancillary studies: forget-coefficient effect, impact of text-conditioning, sensitivity to prior model choice, and an explicit failure-mode analysis (Appendix E.9) showing where prompt/target mismatch causes uncorrectable artifacts — this transparency strengthens credibility.
Good reproducibility: detailed algorithm pseudocode (Alg. 1/2), hyperparameter tables for every task/dataset, explicit baseline configurations, and a stated code release.
weaknesses: The central quantitative story is mixed depending on metric: while LPIPS/PSNR show G2D2 close to continuous baselines, the added FID/KID results in the appendix (Tables 8-11) often show G2D2 noticeably worse than DPS/DDRM (e.g., FFHQ Gaussian deblurring FID 47.7 vs DPS's 24.1), suggesting a real perceptual-quality gap not fully captured by the metrics emphasized in the main text.

Baselines use different pretrained backbones (pixel-domain ADM/ILVR models, Stable Diffusion, LDM-VQ) than G2D2's VQ-Diffusion, and the authors themselves note this 'particularly contributes to the superiority of pixel-domain methods on FFHQ' — this confounds direct comparison of the inverse-problem-solving algorithm itself versus prior-model quality.

Motion-domain results show a large performance gap versus fine-tuned, task-specific baselines (OmniControl, GMD) on trajectory/location error metrics (e.g., Traj. Err 0.272 vs 0.053 for OmniControl), which somewhat undercuts the practical significance of the motion application beyond a proof-of-concept.

Only linear inverse problems and Gaussian measurement noise are studied; nonlinear operators (an important class handled by some continuous-diffusion competitors like DPS/ΠGDM) are explicitly left to future work, narrowing the scope of the claimed contribution.
The ImageNet FID reference set uses only 1000 images (acknowledged as below recommended sample sizes), weakening confidence in FID/KID comparisons on that dataset.

The key substitution in the method (using the pretrained prior p̃θ(z0|zt), trained under the Markov forward process, as a stand-in for qstar(z0|zt) in the variational objective) is justified by the shared marginal q(zt|z0), but the paper does not carefully quantify how well the trained network approximates this true conditional in practice, leaving a gap between the clean theory and the practical approximation quality actually achieved.
